transcript: Birdie
Hi! I help businesses figure out exactly what they need from a chatbot. Before we start — what's your name?
Gary Fenwick

G'day! Gary here, Gary Fenwick, from Suds on Wheels Mobile Dog Grooming. Been doing this six years now, out of Ballarat way. Before that I was at Pampered Paws for nine years, fixed shop, but I got sick of being stuck in the one spot, so I converted an old trailer and went mobile. Best decision I ever made, well, apart from marrying my wife Denise, ha!

Anyway sorry, you asked me name and I've gone off telling you my life story already, that's just how I am, my mate Robbo says I could talk under wet cement. What was it you needed to know?
Birdie
Ha, no worries Gary, I like a good yarn! Six years mobile grooming sounds like a great gig. So tell me — what's the main problem you're hoping a chatbot could solve for Suds on Wheels?
Gary Fenwick

Oh mate, where do I start. Main thing's probably the bookings, honestly. I've got this paper diary right, had it since day one, love the thing, smells like old dog and coffee, but I ALSO got a calendar on me phone that Chloe set up for me years back, and the two of them just don't talk to each other. So I'll book someone in the diary for Tuesday 2pm and then me phone's already got someone else in there for the same slot, and I don't notice till I'm standing out the front of the wrong house wondering where the dog is.

Had a shocker of that back in, oh, must've been March, double booked a poodle and a bloody great big Malamute same time slot, that Malamute took me two and a half hours on its own with the matting, and the poodle lady was not impressed waiting round.

That's the other thing too, people text me at all hours, like 11pm "can you fit Bella in tomorrow" and I don't see it till I'm halfway through someone's dog the next morning and then I feel bad. So yeah — scheduling's the big one I reckon. Something that stops me double booking and maybe handles them odd-hour messages so I'm not glued to me phone at midnight.
Birdie

That double-booking nightmare with the poodle and the Malamute sounds rough, Gary! Sounds like a solid scheduling system would save you a lot of grief. Quick one — right now, how do customers usually get in touch with you to book? Just text messages, or do you get calls, emails, Facebook messages, that sort of thing too?
Gary Fenwick

Yeah nah it's a bit of everything mate. Mostly texts, that's the big one, people just text me straight to me mobile. Then I get some calls too, usually the older folk, they still like to actually ring up and have a chat, which I don't mind, I'm a chatty bugger meself. Got a Facebook page for the business too — Chloe set that up for me, she's good with all that stuff, does me bookings Saturdays when she's helping out — and I get messages through there sometimes, people asking "do you come to Miners Rest" or whatever.

No email really, hardly anyone emails a dog groomer I s'pose, ha. Oh and every now and then someone just flags me down when I'm out in the trailer doing a job, like a neighbour'll come over and go "oi how much to do mine" while I've got me hands full of soapy Labrador. That's a hard one to manage, can't exactly whip out a diary when I'm covered in suds.

So yeah — texts mainly, then calls, then Facebook, then the odd doorstop while I'm elbow deep in a dog. All going into the one paper diary and the one dodgy phone calendar, which is the whole problem really isn't it.
Birdie

Righto, so texts, calls, and Facebook messages all funnelling into that messy diary situation. Do you have any preference for which calendar or booking system the chatbot should work with — like, is Chloe's phone calendar something (Google Calendar, Apple, etc.) we could hook into, or would you rather start fresh with something new?
Gary Fenwick

Oh geez, now you're asking me the hard questions! Honestly mate I couldn't tell you if it's Google or Apple or what, Chloe set the whole thing up on me phone years back, she just said "there Uncle Gary, tap here when someone books" and I've just been tapping ever since, never looked under the bonnet so to speak.

It's one of them iPhones so I'd say it's probably the Apple one, the little calendar icon that's white with the red top, is that Apple? Might be. I really don't know mate, technology's not my strong suit, I can barely work the eftpos machine on the trailer some days, drives Denise mental.

Might be worth asking Chloe honestly, she's the one who'd know what's hooked up to what. But if you're asking me, my gut says just start fresh with whatever's gonna work best and not muck about trying to save my dodgy old calendar, cause half the entries in there are probably wrong anyway knowing me. Long as it's simple enough that I can actually use it without ringing Chloe every five minutes, ha!

Sorry, did that answer it or did I just go round the houses again?
Birdie
That answered it perfectly, Gary — fresh and simple it is, no need to drag Chloe into it. Now, roughly how many bookings or customer messages would you say you handle in an average week?
Gary Fenwick

Ooh, average week, let's think. Depends on the week honestly, spring and summer I reckon I'm flat out, might do fifteen, twenty dogs in a week if the weather's good and everyone wants their dog looking spiffy for the footy finals or whatever's on. Winter it drops off a fair bit, people don't want soggy dogs I s'pose, maybe more like ten, twelve jobs.

Message-wise though, that's a different story, cause not every message turns into a booking. I reckon I get, I dunno, twenty-five, thirty messages a week easy, texts and Facebook and whatnot, half of them's just "how much for a groom" or "do you do cats" — no mate, I do not do cats, learned that lesson the hard way, got scratched to buggery by a Siamese back at Pampered Paws, never again — and then the other half turns into an actual booking.

So yeah, ballpark, maybe dozen or fifteen actual grooms a week, but double or more than that in messages coming at me from all directions. That sound about like what you needed?
Birdie

Good to know, Gary — so a busy-ish operation with lots of 'how much for a groom' questions coming in. Speaking of which, what are your services and prices? Like, do you charge differently by dog size or breed, and what's a standard groom run you?
Gary Fenwick

Oh yeah, plenty to go through here mate, hang on. Right so it's mostly by size, that's the easiest way I found to do it, cause if I tried pricing by breed I'd be here all day arguing with meself about what counts as what, half these dogs are mixed up anyway, "oh he's a bit of everything" the owners say, ha.

So small dog, your Shih Tzus, your little Maltese types, that's a wash and tidy, sixty-five bucks. Medium dog, full groom, that's your Spoodles, Cocker Spaniels, that range, eighty-five to ninety-five depending how much coat they've got going on. Then your big fellas, double-coat breeds, your Malamutes, your Huskies, big fluffy Shepherds, that's one-ten to one-thirty for a full groom.

Now here's where I get a bit sheepish, cause if one of them big double-coat dogs comes to me all matted up — and mate, some of these owners, bless 'em, they let it get away from them something shocking — I honestly don't have a proper system for pricing that. I sort of just look at the dog, have a feel of the coat, go "yeah righto that's gonna be a two-hour job" and pluck a number out that feels fair, which Denise reckons is gonna get me in trouble one day cause I probably undercharge more than I overcharge, I'm too soft.

Then the extras — nail trim on its own is twenty bucks, and deshedding treatment as an add-on, that's another twenty-five on top of whatever groom they're getting.

That's about the size of it! Cats not included, never again, ha.
Birdie

That's really clear, thanks Gary — and good on you for admitting the matted-dog pricing is a bit loose, that's exactly the kind of thing worth nailing down so the chatbot doesn't undersell you. We'll flag that for later. For now, next question: what area do you actually service — like how far out from Ballarat will you drive for a job?
Gary Fenwick

Yeah righto, so I stick pretty close to home base, Ballarat and about a 20km radius round that, that covers me pretty well actually, gets me out to a fair few of them little towns round the edges, Miners Rest, Buninyong, that sort of area.

If it's beyond 15km though I do add on a callout fee, fifteen bucks extra, just cause the diesel in that old van isn't cheap and half me day can go on driving if I'm not careful. Had a bloke once out Snake Valley way, gorgeous big Bernese Mountain Dog mind you, lovely dog, but by the time I drove out there and back I'd near enough burned me whole morning just on the road, so yeah, gotta factor that in.

Anything past that 20km I generally just say sorry mate, bit far for me, cause otherwise I'd be driving to Melbourne for someone's chihuahua, ha. Does that cover what you needed?
Birdie

Perfect, that's really helpful Gary. Now, are there any situations where you'd want the chatbot to stop and hand things over to you directly rather than trying to sort it out itself — like a tricky pricing question, an angry customer, or a same-day emergency booking?
Gary Fenwick

Oh yeah, definitely, mate, there's a few spots where I reckon the bot should just go "righto, this one's above my pay grade, over to Gary." 

Big one's gotta be them heavily matted dogs I was telling you about, cause like I said I don't even know how I price it meself half the time, so no way some computer program's gonna guess it right, it'd probably quote someone sixty bucks for a job that takes me three hours and then I'm cursing me own chatbot, ha. So anything where someone says "oh he's a bit matted" or sends a photo looking like a sheep that's never been shorn, I want that bumped straight to me, I'll ring em and have a proper yarn about it.

Aggressive dogs too, that's a big one, had a Rottweiler a few years back tried to take a chunk out of me arm, lovely owners mind you but the dog had other ideas, so if someone mentions "oh he's a bit funny with strangers" or "he's bitten the last groomer" — mate, straight to me, I need to know what I'm walking into before I turn up solo in me trailer.

Angry customers as well, I don't want no computer trying to smooth over someone who's spewing cause I was running late or whatever, that needs a human touch, or at least Denise, she's better at that than me honestly, calms people right down.

Same-day stuff too probably, them emergency "can you squeeze me in today" messages, cause with the diary and the phone calendar not talking to each other I really need eyes on that before anything gets confirmed, otherwise we're back to Poodle-and-Malamute city all over again.

That answer what you were after?
Birdie

That's really clear, Gary, good instincts on all those handoffs — especially the aggressive dog one, fair enough after that Rottweiler! Last big question: if this chatbot works exactly the way you want in a few months' time, what would that look like for you? Like, what would tell you it's actually working?
Gary Fenwick

Ooh, good question, let's have a think. Honestly mate, if in a few months I'm NOT standing out the front of some poor bugger's house at 2pm wondering where the dog is cause I've double booked meself, that alone I'd call a win, that's probably my number one thing, cause that Poodle-Malamute disaster still haunts me a bit, ha.

Second thing, I reckon if I could actually have a cuppa with Denise of an evening without me phone buzzing every five minutes with "how much for a wash" type questions, that'd be bloody brilliant. Like if the bot's already told 'em the price, told 'em me hours, sorted out is it Tuesday to Saturday, all that basic stuff, and only pings me for the real stuff — the matted dogs, the angry customers, the bitey dogs — then I reckon I'd actually get me evenings back.

And I s'pose if it's working proper, come spring when everyone wants their dog spiffy again, I shouldn't be flat out stressed and disorganised like I usually get, I should just be flat out busy, which is a good kind of tired, not the kind where I'm running round like a chook with its head cut off cause two dogs are booked in the same slot.

So yeah — no double bookings, less midnight texting doing me head in, and me actually trusting the schedule enough that I stop carrying that manky old paper diary around out of habit. That'd tell me it's working. Did I answer it or go off on one again, ha?
Birdie

That's a great answer, Gary, no need to apologize for a good ramble! Sounds like the win is simple: no double bookings, quieter evenings, and you finally trusting the system over that old diary. Last couple of practical ones — do you have a budget in mind for building this chatbot, and any timeline you're hoping to have it up and running by, like before spring gets busy?
Gary Fenwick

Ah righto, budget, this is the bit that gives me a bit of a sweat, ha. I haven't sat down and done proper numbers, Denise keeps telling me I need to "do a budget, Gary, like a real one" but between the grooming and the van and trying to catch the footy on the weekend I never quite get round to it. But if you're twisting me arm for a figure, I reckon not much, maybe a couple hundred bucks a month tops, that's about what I'd be comfortable with without having a small heart attack. Anything more than that I'd have to have a proper sit-down and work out if it's even worth it, cause margins in dog washing aren't exactly footy-star wages, ha.

Timeline-wise, yeah, I'm keen to have something sorted before spring gets flat out, that's when everyone wants their dog looking spiffy. Problem is I'm not even a hundred percent sure when spring "starts" business-wise for me, if you know what I mean — like is it September when it actually ticks over on the calendar, or does it really kick off earlier than that, October, whenever the weather turns nice and everyone starts thinking about it? I always reckon September but then some years it's still freezing and dogs aren't exactly needing a trim for beach season. So somewhere round there, September-ish, but don't hold me to it, I'm not much of a planner as you might've gathered by now!
Birdie

Righto Gary, let me read all that back to you so you can tell me if I've got it straight:

- You're Gary Fenwick from Suds on Wheels Mobile Dog Grooming, Ballarat, mobile trailer setup, dogs only (no cats!).
- Main problem: your paper diary and phone calendar don't talk to each other, causing double bookings (like the infamous Poodle/Malamute day), plus late-night texts catching you off guard.
- Customers reach you by text (the big one), phone calls, and Facebook Messenger.
- You get about 25-30 messages a week, turning into 10-20 actual grooms depending on season.
- Pricing: small dog wash & tidy $65, medium full groom $85-95, large/double-coat full groom $110-130, nail trim alone $20, deshedding add-on $25, callout fee $15 beyond 15km, no service beyond 20km from Ballarat.
- Matted dogs, aggressive dogs, angry customers, and same-day bookings should all get bumped straight to you (or Denise for upset customers).
- Success looks like: no more double bookings, quieter evenings, and trusting the system enough to ditch the paper diary.
- Budget: around $200/month, timeline: ready before spring gets busy, roughly September-ish.

A couple of loose threads for later: confirming your exact operating days (sounds like Tuesday-Saturday?), sorting out a fairer way to price matted dogs, and pinning down an actual launch date. Does all that sound right to you, or is there anything I've got wrong or missed?
Gary Fenwick

Yeah nah mate, that's spot on, you've got me sussed out pretty good there! Just to fill in that loose thread you mentioned — yep, Tuesday to Saturday's me working week, 8 till 4. Monday's meant to be paperwork and van maintenance day but if I'm honest it's mostly just me under the bonnet of the van and the paperwork goes right out the window, ha, don't tell Denise I said that.

Oh and I should mention, Chloe helps me out Saturdays, mainly does the small dogs and handles the texty reception side of things when she's there, so worth keeping in mind for whatever we build, she might end up using it too on her days.

Other than that, yeah, you've nailed it, that's the whole shebang right there! Feeling good about this actually, ha.
Birdie

Beauty, thanks Gary! That's everything I need for now. I'll get this over to the dev team so they can start putting together a chatbot that stops the double-bookings, handles the easy questions for you, and knows exactly when to bump things to you or Denise. We'll follow up on those loose ends — the matted dog pricing, Chloe's access, and locking in a launch date — as we get building. Enjoy that cuppa with Denise tonight, you've earned it after all this yarning!

brief.business_name: Suds on Wheels Mobile Dog Grooming
brief.business_description: Mobile dog grooming service operating out of Ballarat, run by Gary Fenwick for 6 years (previously worked at a fixed-location groomer, Pampered Paws, for 9 years) using a converted trailer. Niece Chloe helps out on Saturdays with small dogs and reception/texts.
brief.problem_to_solve: Double-booking issues from using both a paper diary and a phone calendar that don't sync, causing scheduling conflicts (e.g. double-booked a poodle and a Malamute in March). Also receives late-night text messages from customers wanting bookings, which he doesn't see until the next day, causing delays and stress.
brief.target_audience: Dog owners in and around Ballarat needing mobile grooming services
brief.conversation_volume: Roughly 25-30 customer messages per week (texts, calls, Facebook combined), resulting in about 10-20 actual grooming bookings per week depending on season (busier spring/summer, quieter winter).
brief.success_criteria: No more double-bookings (biggest priority); fewer after-hours/midnight texts interrupting personal time — bot should handle basic questions (pricing, hours, days open) on its own and only escalate real issues (matted dogs, aggressive dogs, angry customers); Gary wants to trust the schedule enough to stop carrying his paper diary; wants to be 'busy but organized' in peak season rather than stressed and double-booked.
brief.budget: Around $200/month (AUD) — Gary's comfortable ceiling without a 'small heart attack'; hasn't done formal budgeting.
brief.timeline: Wants it ready before spring picks up — roughly September, though Gary's unsure of the exact seasonal turning point (could be Sept or Oct depending on weather).
services_and_pricing: Small dog (e.g. Shih Tzu, Maltese) wash and tidy: $65
Medium dog full groom (e.g. Spoodle, Cocker Spaniel): $85-$95 depending on coat
Large/double-coat dog full groom (e.g. Malamute, Husky, Shepherd): $110-$130
Deshedding treatment (add-on): $25 extra on top of groom price
Callout fee of $15 extra for jobs beyond 15km from Ballarat
faq_answers: Does not groom cats — only dogs.
Operating hours: Tuesday to Saturday, 8am to 4pm. Mondays reserved for paperwork/van maintenance (not customer-facing).
business_policies: Services Ballarat and about a 20km radius (covers towns like Miners Rest, Buninyong)
Jobs beyond 15km incur a $15 callout fee
Does not service beyond 20km from Ballarat
Operating days: Tuesday to Saturday, 8am-4pm. Closed Mondays (admin/van maintenance day).
Chloe (Gary's niece) helps on Saturdays with small dog grooming and handling texts/reception — may also use the chatbot system.
escalation_rules: Heavily matted dogs (owner mentions matting or sends photo of matted coat) — escalate to Gary directly, no automated pricing/quote.
Aggressive or reactive dogs (owner mentions dog is 'funny with strangers', has bitten before, etc.) — escalate to Gary so he knows what he's walking into.
Angry or upset customers — escalate to a human (Gary or Denise) rather than have bot attempt to de-escalate.
Same-day/emergency booking requests — escalate for manual confirmation to avoid double-booking conflicts.
open_items: In-person walk-up inquiries while working (e.g. neighbours asking for quotes) are hard to capture digitally — may need a simple way to log these later.
No fixed pricing system for heavily matted double-coat dogs — Gary currently eyeballs it and worries he undercharges. Needs a rule of thumb or pricing tier for matted coat jobs.
Timeline target of 'before spring' is loosely defined (Sept vs Oct) — worth pinning down an actual launch date.
Chloe may need her own access/login to the system on Saturdays — worth clarifying multi-user needs during build.
